rationale: TDD baseline for KAN-181 scope-relevance validation in the Jira agent-label gate. The defect is that cmd_check in scripts/jira_label_gate.py validated agent-* LABEL PRESENCE ONLY, so a stale ticket key that merely carried a label satisfied commit-msg regardless of whether the ticket scope matched the commit; live evidence was a commit whose subject cited KAN-181 while the gate checked a stale KAN-133 left in .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG and printed '[OK] KAN-133 carries agent label'. RED proven at baseline_parent e5fd531f: 25 failed, 1 passed with exit 1, failing on the absent third cmd_check parameter and the absent scope_tokens/scope_overlap helpers. GREEN: 26 passed. The scope mismatch is deliberately a WARNING that still returns 0 rather than a new blocking exit code, because scope matching is heuristic and a false positive must never block legitimate work; the load-bearing exit-code contract (0 = agent label present, 1 = present-but-unlabeled, 2 = cannot verify on missing creds/404/401/403/other) is pinned unchanged by both this suite and the pre-existing 22 tests in tests/test_jira_label_gate.py, which is not edited by this baseline. Coverage includes end-to-end cmd_check wiring, an explicit assertion that fetch_issue is still called exactly once (no new HTTP request), a pure-ASCII output assertion per scripts/AGENTS.md, and not-evaluable guards so a missing summary or a missing commit message never warns. The one test that passes in RED pins the legacy no-message call signature so existing callers keep working unchanged.
